title: Field Trip Vote
story: Your class is voting on a field trip. Each student writes one destination code on a slip: 4 for the aquarium, 9 for the science museum, 17 for the climbing wall, and so on. A trip goes ahead only if one destination gets more than half the votes, and the teacher knows that happened. You need to find the winning destination.
task: Write winningTrip(votes). Return the destination code that appears more than votes.length / 2 times.
Such a destination always exists, so there is always exactly one correct answer.
constraints: One value appears more than votes.length / 2 times.

examples.explanation: There are five votes, so the winner needs at least 3. The science museum, code 9, got 3.
There are seven votes, so the winner needs at least 4. Code 17 got exactly 4, and it does not matter that the first vote was a 4.

hints: With 7 votes, work out how many votes the winner needs. Once a destination reaches that number, no other destination can beat it.
You need each destination's vote count so far, like a tally sheet with one line per destination.
Use a structure that keeps a count per code even when you do not know in advance which codes will appear.
Walk the votes once with a map from code to count. After each vote, if that count is now more than votes.length / 2, return that code.
bruteForce: For each vote, scan the whole box, count the matching slips, and return the first code that is past half. That takes O(n²) time, which is up to 2.5 billion comparisons for 50,000 votes. Sorting also works, since the winner must fill the middle position, but it costs O(n log n) and reorders the slips.

js: * @param {number[]} votes  one destination code per student
* @return {number} the code with more than half the votes

tests.note: winner not first in a row
alternating, winner never twice in a row
first vote is not the winner
winner only appears in the second half
winner bunched at the start, one vote at the end
last vote and middle slip (unsorted) are both losers

js: const count = new Map(); // destination -> votes so far
if (c > votes.length / 2) return v; // nobody can catch up now
return -1; // never reached: a winner always exists
py: if count[v] > len(votes) / 2:  # nobody can catch up now
return -1  # never reached: a winner always exists
walkthrough: The solution reads the slips once and keeps a running tally for each destination. As soon as one destination passes half the class, it has won.
The trace below uses [9, 4, 9, 17, 9]. Half of 5 is 2.5, so the winner needs 3.
• The vote 9 raises the tally for 9 to 1.
• The vote 4 raises the tally for 4 to 1.
• The second vote 9 raises its tally to 2, which is not yet more than 2.5.
• The vote 17 raises the tally for 17 to 1.
• The third vote 9 raises its tally to 3, which is more than 2.5, so the function returns 9.
Compare each tally against the total number of votes, not the number of votes read so far. After the first slip, its destination has 100% of the votes read but has not won.

A solution with O(1) memory also exists, which keeps one candidate and a counter. Add 1 when a vote matches the candidate, subtract 1 when it does not, and switch candidate when the counter hits 0. Each losing vote cancels one winning vote, and the winner outnumbers everyone else combined, so it is left standing.
solution.timeWhy: One pass, with O(1) average work per vote for the map update.
solution.spaceWhy: The map holds one entry per different destination, up to about n / 2 of them.
solution.takeaway: To find the value that occurs most often, or more often than some threshold, keep a hash map of counts while you walk the list. This replaces a full recount for every element with a single update.
